author: Codex documentation author; corrections by DOC-029 source-review author agent (documents)

prerequisites: Signed-in fictional role in its own browser context on the work documentation lab.

Walkthrough-created paper on a Contract (with a Counterparty, a folder, a two-Version Document and an Executed-kind Document), a Matter, an Entity, a Knowledge Item and an Auto-Doc template, all named with DOC-029 documents and a run stamp.
An Administrator-created Confidential Contract whose team is the Administrator alone, as the hidden owner.
scenarios.expected: The repository shows permitted Documents and links to the correct owners/Versions. Hidden owners do not leak through results or filters; archived/empty result behavior matches the guide.
scenarios.actual: 8 recorded browser steps passed for this role. Documents in navigation opened the repository; Recent listed five Documents in the newest-current-Version order and opening an older Document did not add it. Owner offered Contracts, Matters, Entities, Auto-Docs and Knowledge and each choice kept only paper of that owner kind, including the Auto-Doc template. Record with Search choices narrowed to the Contract, Folder then appeared with the folder and Record root, and Knowledge and Auto-Docs offered no Folder. Format with two values matched either; Kind used the current Version; Kind, Counterparty and Uploader together kept only the matching Document; Uploaded From and To on the same day included it and a later From showed "No documents match these filters."; removing one filter and Clear all widened the list, and Recent was hidden while filtered. Selecting a name opened the owning record on the current v2 and the chain opened v1. The Confidential Contract outside this reader's team gave "No matching choices" in Record, was absent from the repository read, and its address answered not found. Filter, Show archived showed the archived row with Restore, which made it live. Dragging a row showed Move to folder for its record and the drop filed it.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the article author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.
Owner-kind checks compared the first page of results (up to 50 rows) with the fixture paper; the shared lab held many other agents' Documents, so full-list totals are not claimed.
Recent was compared with the API's newest-five read at the same moment; parallel uploads by other agents could reorder it between reads, and the script re-read until both matched.
Hidden-owner leakage was checked through Record choices, the repository read and the direct address; Counterparty and Uploader choice lists and saved views were not inspected for the hidden record.
The Uploaded filter used the UTC date of the run, which was the same calendar day in the organization's timezone at the time.
The Business User's refusal of the staff repository is recorded in the document-previews business_user steps.

compatibilityReview.summary: From 3fa407e3 to 57e77e38, round 2 (DOC-029r2 compatibility reviewer (documents)) found the article compatible: I inspected the app diff from 3fa407e3 to 57e77e38 and found no change to Document, Version, folder, preview, repository, archive or delete behavior or labels; the only Document-surface change is the archived uploader color. I replayed the round 1 documents walkthrough on the work2 lab built from 57e77e38, and all 117 steps passed for Administrator, Legal Team Member and Business User. From 57e77e38 to 432dba3a, round 3 found only apps/web/src/routes/welcome.tsx and its test changed. The wizard now goes to /auth/two-factor/enroll after it saves a policy that requires two-factor authentication. The article makes no statement about the setup wizard Authentication step or two-factor enrollment. The change touches only apps/web/src/routes/welcome.tsx and its test, so no statement in the article can become wrong.
